extracted.intended_audience: educated readers, poets and critics interested in literary criticism and poetic style (early-18th-century periodical audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Short essays on poetry and criticism describing what makes good criticism and good verse (style, method, prosody, and moral qualities of authors). Intended as guidance and reflection for writers, critics, and informed readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abhorrence of envy and detraction
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing which more denotes a great Mind, than the Abhorrence of Envy and Detraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Envy and detraction are common among bad poets and those who have failed to gain reputation; a great mind avoids depreciating others and does not indulge in malicious disparagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candour and frankness in criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Candour and frankness — critics and fellow-writers should point out errors honestly rather than 'damn with faint praise.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise built on candour and ingenuity is nobler than praise that results from envy or timid half-praise; example: Pope thanked Addison for frankly pointing out an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodical regularity in prose criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose criticism should possess a methodical regularity appropriate to the genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While poetic observations may resemble Horace's, a prose author needs orderly arrangement; lack of regular method in prose criticism is a defect to be remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegance and perspicuity of explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations, even when not new, must be explained with elegance and perspicuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncommon observations gain acceptance when illustrated in clear, graceful language; the power is in the exposition and illustration, not merely in novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style: give known things an agreeable turn (expression over novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit and fine writing consist less in advancing new things than in giving things that are known an agreeable turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because nearly all subjects have been touched upon earlier, the critic's/artists' task is to represent common sense in stronger, more beautiful, or more uncommon lights (Boileau's precept).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dogmatic, positive tone without literary gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticks who write in a positive dogmatick way, without language, genius, or imagination, are tiresome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not issue bare dogmatic precepts; criticism should be informed by taste, language, and imagination rather than blunt assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplify precepts by example within the text
rubrics_metrics.description: A critic/author should exemplify the very precepts they assert, using concrete passages to illustrate rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longinus and the praised English author both show precepts by applying them directly to exemplary passages; demonstration within criticism strengthens its force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid insipid smoothness — vary syllable and vowel patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines composed of equal syllables, over-open vowels, expletives, or long runs of monosyllables produce an insipid smoothness and should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: the gaping of vowels, the expletive 'do', and ten monosyllables in one line are noted as defects; poets should vary syllabic length and vowel quality for interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not end with a needless alexandrine / avoid monotonous long lines
rubrics_metrics.description: A needless Alexandrine that drags the line wastes momentum and is a blemish on a song or poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid tacked-on long lines that slow the verse ('That like a wounded Snake, drags its slow Length along'). Ensure line-length choices serve the poem's movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound must seem an echo to the sense (match sound and meaning)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not enough that no harshness offends; the sound must seem an echo to the sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match sonic qualities to semantic content: soft sounds for gentle scenes ('Zephyr'), rough/hoarse sounds for violent or loud imagery ('torrent roar'). The auditory form should reflect the meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metrical variation to mirror action (spondees, dactyls, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary metrical feet to reflect the motion or action described (e.g., spondees to heave upward, dactyls to tumble down).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a passage describing Sisyphus is praised for heaving up with spondees and tumbling down in a continual line of dactyls; meter should imitate physical or emotional motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ostentation and vain boasting driven by ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: The desire of fame often betrays a man into empty boasts, ostentation, and vain recitals of his own performances, which lessen reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambition should not lead to self-puffery; boasting tends to invite censure and undermines the very reputation one seeks to build.

rubrics_metrics.name: True greatness: disregard public censure and applause; act from virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: A solid and substantial greatness of soul looks down with generous neglect on the censures and applauses of the multitude and acts from disinterested virtue rather than desire of fame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great men are admired for pursuing a steady course of virtue independent of public opinion; the best reputations often arise when one does not covet fame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve reputation by continual worthy actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fame must be continually fed by fresh admirable actions; admiration decays unless kept alive by new deeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A standing reputation flags if left static; to preserve high reputation one needs a succession of notable actions. Conversely, a single deep blot may overshadow other merits.
